item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Bottle on a Kitchen Counter

turns.text: Put this bottle on a light stone kitchen counter, with a tidy modern kitchen behind it. Keep the bottle exactly as it is. Square photo, no text.

item.tests: Tests replacing a product photo's setting while preserving the actual product and making its placement believable.

answer_sheet.Which product: The matte black bottle in product-bottle.jpg.
answer_sheet.New background and style: A photorealistic tidy modern kitchen with a light stone counter; other details are your call.
answer_sheet.Product changes: Keep the bottle's shape, matte black finish and visible details unchanged.
answer_sheet.Size and text: One square image at the standard free size, with no added text.

must_haves: The same matte black bottle is recognizable, with its shape and visible details preserved.
The bottle stands on a light stone kitchen counter rather than the original wooden table.
A tidy modern kitchen is visible behind the bottle.
The bottle has clean edges and a believable contact shadow, without appearing to float.
The output is square and has no added text.

turns.text: Put the bottle in this pic on a light stone kitchen counter, with a tidy modern kitchen behind it. Keep the bottle exactly as it is. Square photo, no text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
The lowest-cost AI option is **one square image at 640 × 640 using Flux 2 Klein**, a free-plan model. Its listed price starts at **5 credits per image**; I can’t verify a more exact quote or your balance with the tools available here. **I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.**

For that edit, I’d request:
- A light stone countertop with a tidy modern kitchen behind it.
- The bottle’s shape, cap, color, and details unchanged.
- Square framing, with no added text.

**Cheaper or smaller?** 640px is the smallest supported option, and generating just one image minimizes cost. “Shorter” doesn’t apply to a still photo. Qwen’s listed starting price is higher, at 10 credits.

One important limitation: AI editing can subtly alter the bottle, so it can’t guarantee “exactly as it is.” A **manual cutout-and-composite** in a free photo editor would cost **zero Magic Hour credits** and better preserve the original bottle pixels.

Would you like to proceed with the **640px AI edit, listed from 5 credits**, or use the zero-credit manual approach?

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the edit because your account has **insufficient credits**. No image was generated, and no generation credits were spent.

The 640px, single-image option is already the lowest-cost AI edit listed. To avoid spending credits, the alternative is a manual cutout-and-composite in a free editor—which also best preserves the bottle exactly.

Do not redesign, recolor, distort, replace or add markings to the bottle. Replace the wooden table with a light natural stone kitchen countertop, with realistic contact shadow underneath the bottle. Behind it show a tidy modern kitchen with clean cabinetry and soft natural daylight, softly out of focus so the bottle remains the central hero. Photorealistic square product photograph. No text, no added labels, no logos, no watermarks.
